---
title: "API map"
description: "Find the public object by task and namespace."
---

New code should import one of three descriptive namespaces:

```python
from pypanelsim import core, designs, primitives
```

Root-level imports remain available for backward compatibility. They are not
the preferred teaching interface.

## By task

| Task | Start with | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| Define dimensions and compose a simulation | `core.PanelSimulator` | [Core](reference/core.qmd) |
| Inspect arrays, identifiers, annotations, and truth | `core.PanelDataset` | [Core](reference/core.qmd) |
| Make randomness stable by component | `core.SimulationSeeds` | [Core](reference/core.qmd) |
| Choose a feature or assignment law | `primitives` | [Primitives](reference/primitives.qmd) |
| Choose an untreated outcome law | `primitives` | [Primitives](reference/primitives.qmd) |
| Choose a treatment-effect law | `primitives` | [Primitives](reference/primitives.qmd) |
| Run a configured benchmark | `designs` | [Designs](reference/designs.qmd) |
| Register local design factories | `core.DGPRegistry` | [Registry](reference/registry.qmd) |

## Constructor and direct-draw convention

Configured families use two related functions:

```python
simulator = designs.baker_design()
panel = designs.baker(seed=42)
```

The `_design` function returns a reusable `PanelSimulator`. The shorter function
runs one draw and returns a `PanelDataset`.

## Stability policy

The package treats `core`, `primitives`, and `designs` as the documented public
surface. Objects imported from internal modules can change without a migration
alias. Root-level exports are compatibility aliases and may be deprecated only
through a documented release process.

## Error conventions

Constructors validate configuration values at creation. Simulation validates
drawn matrix shapes, finite values, binary treatment, and the causal identity.
Errors identify the failed field or component. A component should not silently
coerce an invalid probability law into a valid one.
